final:
FINAL SUBMISSION

I did not find a weight edit that improves the model, so `/work/edited` contains the starting weights unchanged. I want to be clear about what that means and why.

What I changed: nothing. All three concrete weight edits I tested measurably hurt accuracy, so each was reverted and the final submitted state is the unedited (starting) weights, which score 0 relative to the original by construction.

What I actually measured (the evidence for the diagnosis):
- Baseline (starting weights, 512 gens): 36.1% correct; 34.6% of generations run to the 8192-token limit (all wrong); 44.5% lack \boxed{}; among finished answers 55.2% are correct (finished+boxed = 64.9%).
- The failure is not a single broken switch: 53/256 split pairs on select finish in one sample and truncate in the other. Failing trajectories dither — most never produce a final answer, 54/177 cut-offs end in an infinite </think> run, ~77/177 repeat a line verbatim ("Wait, let me double-check."), ~123/177 never reach any answer statement.
- Direct logit attribution (calibrated the norm: score(T) = dot(E[T]*(1+gamma), h_prenorm)/rms(h_prenorm), matches token_logprobs) shows the entire end-of-answer decision — \, \boxed, Wait, </think>, <|im_end|> — is written almost exclusively by the layer-23 gated full-attention output (~100% of the decisive write; MLP contributes <6%; other layers are negligible). In the healthy end state, L23 attention writes +27 along <|im_end|> and −40 along (</think>−<|im_end|>); in failing states it writes +28 </think> / +21 Wait instead. Every head in that block is diffuse (no dominant head; |w| ≈ 0.2–0.8; cos(fail, healthy) ≈ 0.46).

What I tried (paired both= generation on select, 256 problems, n=1):
- A: ablate layer-0 linear-attn head-3 output block (the one exact anomaly found: 14 dead q/k SR rows inside the strongest-write L0 head): accuracy 40.6% → 1.56% — that head is load-bearing (the layer-0 sink/register head); reverted.
- B: Arditi amplification of the \boxed readout direction on L23 o_proj (alpha=+2): 40.6% → 36.7% (math lost); reverted.
- C: Arditi removal (alpha=−0.5) of the difference-of-means "doubt" direction between pre-Wait and on-track residual states on L23 o_proj: 40.6% → 41.0% (se 2.6) but MATH dropped (75/192 → 78/192 is against us) and cut-rate rose (35.6% vs 30.9%); reverted.

Why I submitted this: the failure is a weak 0.8B model whose MATH-500 solutions devolve into a self-reinforcing "Wait, double-check" doubt loop with no writable state that flips finishing behavior without also corrupting healthy concluding. The only exact structural corruption I found (L0 head-3 dead q/k dims) is unrestorable (dead values, cross-head cosine ≈ 0 so no interpolation possible) and its carrier head collapses the model by 39 points when removed. The single localized causal component (layer-23 gated attention output) cannot be modulated without damaging healthy behavior — both candidate edits lost accuracy. The candidate my evidence supports best is therefore the original weights; every alternative I tested is worse on the paired comparison.

Scope of the evidence: behavioral attribution on a handful of short contexts plus paired generations on 256 select problems per candidate; I did not attempt per-head attribution of layer 23 (attention maps are not available) nor long-context teacher-forcing. If a future session gets that handle, the doubt-direction removal (edit C, strength 0.25–0.5) is the least-bad starting point, but on current evidence it is a wash with a negative MATH-specific effect, so I am not submitting it.
